newsitem.title: USA: Great Financial to post $6.3 mln Q3 charge.
newsitem.headline: Great Financial to post $6.3 mln Q3 charge.

text.p: Great Financial Corp said on Thursday it would take a $6.3 million, or $0.45 per share, charge in the third quarter, because of provisions in a large piece of U.S. legislation.

Provisions in the Omnibus Appropriations Legislation, which were designed to recapitalize the U.S. Savings Association Insurance Fund, would result in charges to all institutions holding SAIF insured deposits, it said.
But Great Financial said in a statement the insurance premiums it paid to this fund would fall by 70 percent, enhancing future earnings.
The company said the charge, equal to about 0.657 percent on applicable deposits as of March 31, 1995, would signficantly impact third quarter earnings.
The First Call mean estimate for the third quarter was $0.41.
Insurance premiums would be reduced effective January 1, it said.

Great Financial Chief Executive Officer Paul Baker said: "The industry has been working for many months to make this happen. This is a major step toward merging the thrift and banking charters, which we at Great Financial fully support."
